faqs.a:
(a)
For purposes of time, economy, and to facilitate the progress of the hearing, upon
               either party's request or at the hearing officer's direction, the hearing officer
               shall conduct a pre-hearing conference with both parties for the purpose of resolving
               procedural matters or discussing motions filed by the parties.
(b)
A pre-hearing conference shall be informal and must be conducted by the hearing officer.
               The conference need not be recorded, but any rulings, orders, directives, stipulations
               or agreements arrived at or tendered therein shall be made a part of the hearing record.
               No final decision on the ultimate issue of the hearing shall be tendered by the hearing
               officer at any pre-hearing conference.
(c)
Either party may file preliminary motions with the hearing officer concerning the
               admissibility of evidence, notice of the proceeding, bias or qualification of the
               hearing officer, or any other matter concerning the procedure or course of conduct
               of the hearing. The hearing officer may rule upon such motions at any time, up to
               and including the date of the hearing, but may not, based solely upon such preliminary
               motion, rule on any such motion which purpose or effect is to decide the ultimate
               issue of the hearing. The ultimate issue may only be decided upon by the hearing officer
               at the completion of the hearing.
(d)
Any preliminary matter shall be taken up on motion by either party submitted to the
               hearing officer not less than five business days prior to the hearing. Any motion
               submitted by a party less than five business days prior to the hearing, unless submitted
               as a response to a motion filed not less than ten business days prior to the hearing,
               may be stricken and disregarded by the hearing officer if to rule upon the motion
               would unduly delay the progress of the hearing, or constitute an unfair surprise and
               burden on the nonmoving party. For cause, the hearing officer may permit motions to
               be filed later than five days prior to the hearing, but shall give due consideration
               to any request by the nonmoving party for continuance so that a response may be filed.
(e)
The parties shall serve each other with copies of any motion submitted to the hearing
               officer at the same time the hearing officer is served. Facsimile transmission shall
               suffice for such purpose. Provided, however, that facsimile transmissions sent after
               5:00 p.m. or on the weekend shall be deemed to be sent on the next business day for
               purposes of this section. Unless excused for good cause, the hearing officer shall
               strike and disregard any preliminary motion not served upon the other party. The hearing
               officer shall give due consideration to any motion for continuance arising out of
               a party's failure to timely serve the other party with any preliminary motion.
(f)
Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions, the hearing officer may rule on any preliminary
               motion regarding the timeliness of the appeal at any time, up to and including the
               date of the hearing.
(Code 1981, § 2-146; Ord. No. 3608, §§ 1, 2, 4-3-2003)
